:::{#thm-contradiction-works}
#### Why a proof by contradiction works

For [propositions](#def-proposition) $P$ and $C$,

$$
P \equiv \paren{\neg P \Rightarrow (C \land \neg C)}.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

By the definitions of [and](#def-and) and [not](#def-not),
$C \land \neg C$ is false in every row,
so it is a [contradiction](#def-contradiction).
So, by the definition of [implies](#def-implies),
$\neg P \Rightarrow (C \land \neg C)$ is true exactly in the rows
where $\neg P$ is false,
which are the rows where $P$ is true:

| $P$ | $C$ | $\neg P$ | $C \land \neg C$ | $\neg P \Rightarrow (C \land \neg C)$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| T | T | F | F | T |
| T | F | F | F | T |
| F | T | T | F | F |
| F | F | T | F | F |

The first and last columns match in every row,
so the two are [logically equivalent](#def-logically-equivalent).

:::

:::
